name: Postie Bike
summary: R123's Postie Bike, rebuilt against its contact sheet in br-bwju.11: a bent leg shield with bowed facets and a floor wedge with rubber pads; lugged tyres on black four-diameter spoked wheels; an octagon headlamp with rim and lens; swept silver bars with black grips and round mirrors on stalks; twin hex mufflers with header pipes and shocks; a front mudguard with skirts; a silver wire carrier with a postal-red mail tub and parcels; open-top panniers with lid rims and parcels; a rounded rear grab rail, tail block with brake cap and hex lens. The rider is part of the model: faceted white helmet with a grey lower ring and a clear visor frame, hi-vis vest with bands and stripes, puffy blue sleeves, shorts and tall boots. LOD0 2782 triangles (qualified budget now 3000). The physics hulls are frozen at the br-bwju.5 bake.
feedback: Comment on this page (what to change, which view or state); the session turns each comment into a bug bead that cites this page and the car's id.

reference.note: Left to right per view: the reference, the model rendered from the same view, and the silhouette diff (green is model outside the reference, red is reference the model misses). Scored with the helmet-patched masks and the level far camera of refs/sheets.json; thin parts (wire basket, rail, mirror stalks) vanish from the masks on both sides.

damage.note: Left to right: intact; front and back loose; the rider loose; wheel_F cambered; front detached; the rider thrown (detached, R121); back detached; wheel_F detached; rider and front detached; a stripped frame. Posed in a three.js viewer about each part's hinge line (tools/vehicles/evidence).

paints.pattern: Seat colour on the paint key (the leg shield, side covers and mudguards tint); the postal-red panniers, the hi-vis vest and the parcels keep their colours, so it reads as a postie in any seat colour. The number sits on the rider's back (anchor roof_number) and in the HUD badge.

findings.text: contract + reproducibility (origin between the axles; anchors unchanged; mass fractions unchanged; part set core, front, back, rider, wheel_F, wheel_R at every LOD)

silhouette: weighted IoU LOD0 0.7999 -> 0.8579 (side 0.757 -> 0.850, top 0.887 -> 0.846, front 0.793 -> 0.868, rear 0.747 -> 0.893); LOD1 0.7502 -> 0.8441; LOD2 0.685 -> 0.7827. Below the skill's ~0.95: thin parts (wire basket, rail, mirror stalks, spokes) vanish from the masks, the sheet's panniers and bars are wider than the sim's bike, and the top view got worse (0.887 -> 0.846) because the sheet's plan is perspective-stretched

paint key / one material; draws per tile unchanged (44 in the mixed grid); the shield, floor, body, mudguards and tail block tint, the panniers, vest and parcels keep their colours
damage states (damage-strip.png: front, back and the rider swing about their hinge lines, wheels detach, the rider is thrown; no see-through holes)
physics fit (colliders.png: one convex hull per part, as it was; the new panniers, bars, mirrors and helmet are not collision surfaces)
wheel size: the sheet's tyres are about 0.37 m in radius, the model's 0.4 m and 0.36 m (the sim's)
